blurb: A `requires` clause is checked on entry, before the function has returned anything, so `result` is not bound there. Only an `ensures` can read it. Either state the condition over the parameters, or, if it is a claim about the return value, make it an `ensures`. A parameter that is itself named `result` is read as that parameter.
example:
fn inc(x: Int) -> Int
  requires small: result < 100    // ✗ nothing has been returned yet

fn inc(x: Int) -> Int
  ensures small: result < 100     // ✓ checked on exit
summary: A precondition (`requires`) references `result`; the return value is only in scope inside an `ensures`.
